headline: Perturbation and representation models gain structure from additive baselines, linear decompositions and causal links
label: Structured Perturbation Response Modeling
summary: Eight preprints test how much structure perturbation and single-cell models need, from linear and additive baselines to causal latents and curated-annotation probes.
synthesis: Most items address single-cell perturbation response prediction and ask how much explicit structure is needed. BiPert splits responses into shared and perturbation-specific linear parts for unseen perturbations. GAIN models combinatorial responses as an additive baseline plus a learned interaction term. CIRCE places Boltzmann distributions over Hamming distance in combinatorial perturbation space to infer graded signaling activity. CMC-VAE links genes and proteins in a causal latent space from CITE-seq data, and an inverse-perturbation GNN uses integrated gradients to attribute target nominations. Two items probe representations: curated annotations benchmark ESMC layers, neurons and SAEs, and a study asks whether single-cell foundation models need 512 dimensions to encode count values. SimpleP2G is a pathology-to-expression outlier. The shared direction is constrained, interpretable modeling, not a uniform method.
